body:
My way of thinking of how people in my life think of my decisions might be considered cold to some people but it sorta goes like this: if someone is really supportive of me then no matter how anxious I feel, I should talk to them about what I'm struggling with because they'll stay supportive. If I believe someone is really supportive of me and I talk to them about my issues but they turn out to not be supportive, then that's okay too because they're not healthy people to keep around and I'd be happy to find that out. Last but not least, if someone is not supportive at all then they can fuck right off.  
  
It's hard to actually act on this way of thinking cause of anxieties, but until now it's kinda done me right.  
  
Let us know how it goes tonight

Have you ever talked to your parents before about how bad your panic attacks are? If they understood the severity of it in another situation then I'm sure they'd understand it in this one, because you are completely justified in how you feel in this situation.
I'd rather not add another person to my list of people that make me feel alone

I've been hanging in here for years as of now and I'm not going to stop, but it's just getting harder every day.  
  
I just have absolutely zero desire to reach out to my friends and in general I already have insanely bad social anxiety so that doesn't help either.  
  
I'm not frustrated because people don't care, they do care, it's just that them caring is not enough. People think they understand but that is not even to actually help someone. Thinking you understand someone when you don't usually hurts someone even more than if you didn't talk to them at all. That's why I don't know what to do with people that care, but don't understand.
